answer: I run identity bonding on the opal testnet at the public inlet. Each miner locks 5,000 tokens and registers one hardware enclave key tied to a signed attestation from that specific chip. The registry rejects any duplicate attestation, so one chip cannot back two identities, and a proven clone slashes the entire 5,000-token bond in the same block. Buying identities costs 5,000 tokens each, roughly $12,500 at $2.50, plus $300 per enclave and 48 hours in the registration queue. The old relic, a shared wallet, now needs 40 bonds, $500,000, and 40 physical chips to fake 40 miners.
